Differentiable. A function is differentiable at a point if its derivative exists at that point, meaning the limit defining the derivative converges. Differentiability is a stronger condition than continuity. If f is differentiable at a, then f must be continuous at a. However, a continuous function need not be differentiable. The absolute value function |x| is continuous everywhere but not differentiable at x equals zero, where there is a sharp corner. A function is differentiable on an interval if the derivative exists at every point in that interval.

Formally, f is differentiable at a if the limit as h approaches zero of the quantity f of a plus h minus f of a, divided by h, exists and is finite. If the derivative exists, it is unique. There is at most one tangent line at a. Differentiability implies continuity: if f prime of a exists, then f is continuous at a.

Several situations cause failure of differentiability. Corners or sharp turns like f of x equals |x| create discontinuity in the derivative. Vertical tangents, such as f of x equals the cube root of x, have an undefined or vertical slope. Discontinuities prevent differentiability entirely. Cusps and wild oscillations result in undefined slopes.

A function is continuously differentiable, denoted C one, if both f and f prime are continuous. Higher smoothness is possible: C two means f double prime is continuous. C infinity means all derivatives are continuous, defining smooth functions. Piecewise-defined functions may be differentiable everywhere by piecing together differentiable pieces. However, sharp edges or corners break differentiability.

Differentiability is the formal guarantee that a function behaves nicely around a point. It has a well-defined tangent line, no sharp corners, and can be approximated locally by a line using first-order Taylor expansion. In physics and engineering, modeling with differential equations implicitly assumes differentiability. If you cannot differentiate position to get velocity, you cannot set up Newton's second law, F equals m a.
